strengths: Well-motivated insight connecting aesthetic objectives to spatial compute allocation, with clear demonstration of aesthetics-driven spatial non-uniformity in denoising
Comprehensive and rigorous experimental validation: 10,000 prompts, 30,000 images, unified implementation, multiple quality metrics, extensive ablations across three modern DiT architectures
Strong empirical results: 2.11× speedup on Lumina-Next with +11.9% ImageReward improvement, consistent gains across multiple architectures and metrics
Training-free and practical approach applicable to deployed systems without retraining; clear presentation with informative figures and detailed appendices
Thorough ablations (Figs. 4-5, Tables 7-10) clearly demonstrate complementarity of spatial and temporal components, with transparent runtime decomposition
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components (spatial masking from cross-attention, step-level caching, spatial CFG) are well-established; primary contribution is their combination rather than fundamental innovation

Architecture-dependent implementation reduces generalization claims: SD3-Medium disables spatial CFG due to instability; FLUX.1-dev uses only temporal acceleration; raises questions about robustness and architectural constraints

Fixed 34-word anchor vocabulary is manually curated and covers only 65.48% of evaluation prompts; no principled justification for anchors, no comparison to data-driven or learned alternatives, and fallback behavior for uncovered prompts unexplored

Evaluation bias and limited scope: uses Pick-a-Pic dataset with high aesthetic descriptor prevalence, no human evaluation studies, only automatic metrics (ImageReward trained on same Pick-a-Pic data), generalization to non-aesthetic prompts and other datasets unknown

Temporal acceleration oversimplified: one-shot mask at step 5 assumes stable salient regions; linear extrapolation between two cached steps is crude without exploring higher-order alternatives; hyperparameter sensitivity (skip_ratio, mask_step) suggests brittleness

Incomplete code availability reference ('available at .') and unresolved architectural constraints: no clear explanation for why spatial CFG destabilizes SD3-Medium or principled guidelines for adapting to new architectures

Lack of theoretical analysis: no formal characterization of when/why spatial non-uniformity holds or how to predict applicability to new models; missing analysis of failure modes and conditions causing degradation

strengths: Strong empirical results: achieves 2.11× speedup on Lumina-Next while improving ImageReward by +11.9%, with consistent gains across three DiT backbones and statistically validated human preference study (p<0.001)
Well-motivated insight connecting aesthetic-driven spatial non-uniformity to computation allocation, with clear intuitive appeal and extensive cross-attention visualization evidence

Exceptional experimental rigor: comprehensive baselines, multiple complementary metrics, statistically significant human study (15 annotators, 60 pairs), thorough ablations, and robustness checks across scene types and descriptor-free prompts
Exceptional transparency: detailed hyperparameters, full 34-anchor vocabulary, backbone-specific adaptations, runtime decomposition, and extensive sensitivity analyses enabling reproducibility
Practical value: training-free method with low overhead (0.18s for AesMask construction) that improves both efficiency and quality—rare and valuable trade-off
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: combines existing techniques (CLIP similarity matching, sparse attention with global keys, linear extrapolation) primarily as engineering contribution rather than introducing new algorithms or theoretical insights

Generalization concerns from fixed aesthetic anchor vocabulary: only 44.9% coverage on full Pick-a-Pic unique set (vs. 65.48% on evaluation subset), no mechanism for domain adaptation, and unclear performance on non-English or non-aesthetic-heavy domains

Architecture-specific constraints reduce claimed generality: spatial CFG disabled for SD3-Medium, FLUX.1-dev doesn't support spatial SkipSparse path (temporal-only), suggesting method requires careful per-architecture tuning rather than being universally applicable

Insufficient justification for claimed spatial-temporal coupling: paper asserts they are 'coupled' but provides primarily empirical observation; lacks formal analysis of why aesthetic token attention should correlate with temporal predictability

Ad-hoc failure mitigation: acknowledged failures on diffuse-attention prompts (dense crowds, abstract art); recovery via late-mask and entropy fallbacks (92.7–95.4%) lacks principled justification, suggesting core assumptions don't universally hold

Hyperparameter sensitivity and potential dataset bias: multiple interdependent hyperparameters (mask_step, skip_ratio, refresh interval) tuned to Pick-a-Pic (which is biased toward aesthetic descriptors); unclear generalization to other prompt distributions

Limited temporal prediction sophistication: StepCache uses simple linear extrapolation without exploring more sophisticated temporal modeling; correlation of predictions across timesteps not formally analyzed
Evaluation scope limitations: single resolution (1024×1024), single GPU (RTX 5090), only recent DiT variants; generalization to other hardware and older architectures uncertain
